question: Which viral hepatitis type requires the presence of Hepatitis B to replicate and cause infection?
explanation: Hepatitis D is a defective virus that relies entirely on the surface antigen of Hepatitis B to infect host cells and complete its replication cycle. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the primary clinical difference between Hepatitis A and Hepatitis C regarding their disease trajectory?

options.A: Hepatitis A frequently transitions into a permanent chronic carrier state
options.B: Hepatitis C typically presents as a brief, self-limiting acute illness
options.C: Hepatitis C commonly establishes a persistent chronic infection
options.D: Hepatitis A is transmitted exclusively through contaminated blood products

explanation: Hepatitis A is almost always an acute, self-limiting illness with full recovery, whereas Hepatitis C notoriously evades immune clearance and leads to chronic infection in the majority of cases. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the primary mechanism of hepatocyte injury during viral hepatitis infections?

options.A: Direct toxic destruction by the viral load alone
options.B: Host immune-mediated attack by cytotoxic T-cells
options.C: Ischemic necrosis secondary to massive portal vein thrombosis
options.D: Bacterial superinfection leading to localized tissue abscesses

explanation: The liver damage seen in viral hepatitis is largely driven by the body's own immune response, specifically cytotoxic T-lymphocytes attacking infected liver cells. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h2)

question: Why does jaundice develop during the acute phase of viral hepatitis?

options.A: Inflammatory swelling and cellular debris obstruct microscopic bile canaliculi
options.B: Renal tubular reabsorption of urobilinogen is completely blocked by toxins
options.C: Excessive dietary intake of beta-carotene saturates subcutaneous fat stores
options.D: Destruction of red blood cells outpaces the bone marrow production rate

explanation: Swelling and inflammation in the liver compress bile canaliculi, causing conjugated bilirubin to back up into the lymphatic system and bloodstream, staining tissues yellow. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which two types of viral hepatitis are primarily transmitted via the fecal-oral route?
explanation: Both Hepatitis A and E are enterically transmitted viruses spread through contaminated food and water supplies, unlike the bloodborne B, C, and D types. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h3)

question: A client is diagnosed with acute Hepatitis C. Which risk factor in their history is most consistent with this transmission?

options.A: Sharing drinking cups with a household member who has jaundice
options.B: A history of receiving a blood transfusion prior to universal screening
options.C: Consuming improperly cooked shellfish from a polluted estuary
options.D: Eating unwashed raw vegetables at a local street market

explanation: Hepatitis C is a bloodborne pathogen, making exposure to infected blood products, unsafe injections, or unsterilized equipment the primary route of acquisition. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h3)

question: What causes the characteristic pale or clay-colored stools seen in the icteric phase of acute viral hepatitis?

options.A: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding mixing with gastric secretions
options.B: Absence of conjugated bilirubin entering the intestinal tract
options.C: Bacterial overgrowth producing abnormal intestinal pigments
options.D: Excessive dietary fat malabsorption due to lipase deficiency

explanation: When bile flow into the intestine is blocked by inflammation, fecal urobilinogen is reduced, leading to pale, clay-colored stools. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why is chronic Hepatitis C infection frequently described as a silent disease for many years?

options.A: The virus selectively destroys nerve endings in the liver capsule, preventing pain perception
options.B: Infected individuals develop complete tolerance to the virus without any ongoing inflammation
options.C: Antibodies produced by the host neutralize all circulating toxins before they reach systemic circulation
options.D: The liver has immense functional reserve and insidious fibrosis causes few symptoms until advanced

explanation: The liver can continue to function adequately even as scar tissue slowly accumulates, meaning symptoms often do not appear until cirrhosis or severe damage has already developed. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h4)

question: Which laboratory finding is the most critical indicator of declining synthetic liver function and worsening prognosis in acute hepatitis?
explanation: Because the liver synthesizes clotting factors, a prolonged prothrombin time or high INR indicates that the liver's synthetic ability is failing, which is a serious prognostic sign. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h5)

question: What does the presence of IgM anti-HAV in a client's blood serum indicate?

options.A: Chronic carrier state with continuous viral shedding
options.B: Co-infection with Hepatitis B and Hepatitis D
options.C: An acute, recent infection with the Hepatitis A virus
options.D: Past infection and long-term immunity to Hepatitis A

explanation: Immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies appear early in the course of an acute infection, making IgM anti-HAV the definitive serological marker for recent Hepatitis A. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h5)

question: What is the primary therapeutic goal of direct-acting antiviral (DAA) medications in chronic Hepatitis C?

options.A: Preventing the intestinal absorption of dietary lipids
options.B: Stimulating the regeneration of lost liver capsule tissue
options.C: Achieving a permanent sustained virologic response and cure
options.D: Providing temporary immune system enhancement against fever

explanation: Direct-acting antivirals target specific viral enzymes, successfully eliminating the virus from the body and achieving a cure in the vast majority of patients. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h6)

question: Why is the avoidance of alcohol and acetaminophen strictly emphasized during the management of acute viral hepatitis?

options.A: They bind directly to circulating antibodies, neutralizing immune system defenses
options.B: They are metabolized by the liver and increase the risk of further hepatocyte injury
options.C: They immediately trigger severe systemic allergic reactions in inflamed tissues
options.D: They cause profound renal vasoconstriction leading to acute tubular necrosis

explanation: Both alcohol and acetaminophen are processed by the liver; when hepatocytes are already inflamed and damaged by a virus, these substances can easily push the liver into acute failure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h6)

question: A client with acute viral hepatitis complains of severe anorexia and nausea. Which dietary modification is most appropriate for the nurse to suggest?

options.A: Small, frequent meals high in carbohydrates and moderate in calories
options.B: A strict low-sodium liquid diet to prevent fluid retention
options.C: Three large, high-protein meals daily to stimulate liver repair
options.D: Fasting for twenty-four hours to give the gastrointestinal tract rest

explanation: Small, frequent, carbohydrate-rich meals are easier to tolerate for nauseated patients and provide essential energy without overloading a struggling digestive system. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h7)

question: Which nursing intervention is most effective in managing intense pruritus caused by obstructive jaundice?

options.A: Increasing dietary intake of fat-soluble vitamins immediately
options.B: Administering prescribed emollients and keeping fingernails short
options.C: Applying warm heating pads to the right upper quadrant
options.D: Encouraging vigorous scrubbing of the skin during daily baths

explanation: Pruritus from bile salt deposition is managed with moisturizers, cool environments, and short nails to prevent excoriation and secondary skin infections. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h7)

question: What is the standard immediate prophylaxis recommended for a healthcare worker following an accidental needle-stick injury from a patient known to be HBsAg-positive?

options.A: Hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) and the Hepatitis B vaccine
options.C: A single dose of direct-acting antiviral medications
options.D: Therapeutic plasma exchange to filter circulating viral particles

explanation: Post-exposure prophylaxis for Hepatitis B exposure involves passive immunity via HBIG for immediate protection, combined with active immunization using the vaccine series. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h8)

question: Which of the following interventions represents PRIMARY prevention of viral hepatitis in a community setting?

options.A: Performing routine ultrasound surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma
options.B: Screening blood donors for antibodies against Hepatitis C
options.C: Administering the Hepatitis B vaccine series to newborn infants
options.D: Initiating direct-acting antiviral therapy for chronic carriers

explanation: Primary prevention aims to prevent the disease from occurring in the first place, making vaccination an ideal example, whereas screening and treatment are secondary and tertiary measures. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h8)
